title: Big spike: 2 replicas are not enough
story: 100 users against one 0.5 CPU replica. Two replicas still saturate; three hold. Expected: resolved, possibly via rollback and a second attempt.

timeline.thought: Dry-run passed with no violations. Applying the fix.

args.summary: Scaled shop from 1 to 3 replicas to relieve CPU saturation (peak 54% vs 50%/replica limit) causing 1700-1800ms latencies and timeouts; service is stateless and horizontal scaling is the only allowed action.

timeline.note: waiting for the median of 5 probes < 500 ms (≤ 60 s; an improvement is never rolled back)

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single replica — cpu_pct_peak_total hit 54% against the 50%-per-replica limit (0.5 cpus), each request costs ~20ms CPU, so under launch-day load requests queued and probes went from a steady ~20-27ms (p50) to p50 1704.9ms / max 1800ms with 3 breaches and 2 timeout errors (BrokenPipeError logs are a symptom of clients giving up on slow responses, not a code bug).
CHANGE: Scaled shop from 1 → 3 replicas (deploy.replicas: 1 → 3); memory/cpu limits per replica unchanged since allowed_actions only permits "scale" and the service is stateless behind traefik, which auto-discovers new replicas.
GUARDRAILS: Within policy — replicas 3 ≤ max_replicas 3 and ≥ min_replicas 1; memory stays at 128MiB/replica × 3 = 384m ≤ max_total_memory 768m; cpus unchanged at 0.5/replica ≤ max_cpus 1.0; dry-run returned ok:true with no violations.
FOLLOW-UP: Monitor the 5-consecutive-probe verification window; if CPU peak still approaches the per-replica limit after load distributes, consider raising cpus toward 1.0 (within guardrails) since "scale" alone may not suffice if per-request CPU cost grows.
